results.title: Henry III of France stabbed by assassin
results.description: King Henry III of France was stabbed this day in 1589 by Jacques Clément, a Jacobin friar, and died the next day after acknowledging his Bourbon ally, Henry of Navarre (Henry IV), a Huguenot, as his successor.

results.title: Fahd, Saudi Arabia King, Succeeded by Abdullah
results.description: Fahd, who became king of Saudi Arabia in 1982, died at age 82; he was succeeded by his half brother ʿAbd Allah

results.title: George R.R. Martin Publishes A Game of Thrones
results.description: American author George R.R. Martin published A Game of Thrones, the first installment in his hugely popular fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire

results.title: Mike Tyson Becomes Undisputed Heavyweight Champion in 1987
results.description: American boxer Mike Tyson defeated Tony Tucker and was unanimously recognized as the undisputed heavyweight champion by all three sanctioning organizations (WBC, WBA, IBF) in 1987.

results.title: Launch of MTV Cable Network
results.description: The cable television network MTV debuted, with the broadcast of the music video for Video Killed the Radio Star by the Buggles

results.title: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir Elected First Woman Head of State
results.description: Icelandic teacher and politician Vigdís Finnbogadóttir became president of Iceland; she was the first woman in the world to be elected head of state in a national election

results.title: 1966 University of Texas Clock Tower Shooting
results.description: Charles Whitman, a student and ex-marine, fired down from the clock tower on the campus of the University of Texas at Austin, killing 14 people and wounding 31 others (one of whom died years later from complications related to his wounds); it was one of the worst mass murders in a public area in U.S. history. Watch a video of Neal Spelce, who reported live on the 1966 shooting, describing the response to the event AP Images

results.title: 1944 Warsaw Uprising Against German Occupation
results.description: The Warsaw Uprising began in 1944 as the Polish resistance tried to liberate Warsaw from German occupation before the advancing Soviet army arrived. After fierce fighting, the Poles were forced to surrender in October due to lack of supplies and reinforcements.

results.title: Final diary entry of Anne Frank, Holocaust victim
results.description: The final entry was recorded in the diary of Anne Frank, a young Jewish girl who spent two years hiding from the Nazis in Amsterdam before being arrested and dying in a concentration camp.

results.title: John F. Kennedy's Book "Why England Slept" Published in 1940
results.description: John F. Kennedy's Why England Slept, a critical account of the British military that became a best seller, was published

results.title: 1936 Berlin Olympics Showcased Nazi Ideology and Jesse Owens
results.description: The Summer Olympics opened in Berlin, and the efforts by Adolf Hitler and the Nazi Party to demonstrate the superiority of the "Aryan race" were undermined by the success of African American athletes, notably Jesse Owens. Olympic history quiz AP

results.title: Colorado Becomes 38th U.S. State
results.description: Colorado was admitted to the union, becoming the 38th U.S. state

results.title: Birth of American Author Herman Melville
results.description: American writer Herman Melville—best known for his novels of the sea, most notably Moby Dick (1851)—was born

results.title: Birth of Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, French Biologist
results.description: Jean-Baptiste Lamarck, a French biologist best known for his theory of the inheritance of acquired traits, was born in the village of Bazentin-le-Petit in 1744.

results.title: Queen Anne of England Dies at Age 49
results.description: Queen Anne, the last monarch from the House of Stuart, died in 1714 at the age of 49. Her death marked the end of the Stuart dynasty's rule over England.

results.title: Birth of Roman Emperor Claudius I
results.description: Roman Emperor Claudius I was born in Lugdunum, Gaul (now Lyon, France) in 10 BCE. He went on to extend Roman rule in North Africa and make Britain a province.
